items.title: Prompt-injection defence depth (Turing College review finding)
items.description: Defences rely on deterministic heuristics in src/security.py and on RAG prompt instructions. Extend detection with a labelled regression corpus (direct, indirect, multilingual, encoded, retrieved-document), measure detection and benign false positives, fail CI on regression against an approved held-out corpus, add an injection-risk score to each RetrievalResult, quarantine high-risk chunks before context construction, revalidate every model-requested tool action against the authenticated user's goal, authorization, tool permissions and allowed arguments before any side effect, keep output-side safeguards in answer(), and never rely solely on the LLM obeying an instruction.
items.acceptance_criteria: R1 corpus derived from evaluations/jailbreak_test_results.csv covering direct, indirect, multilingual, encoded and retrieved-document attacks, with a frozen held-out split; R2 attack detection rate and benign false-positive rate are measured and reported per language; CI fails below the owner-approved thresholds (OD-GATE-THRESHOLDS); R3 every RetrievalResult carries an injection-risk score; chunks above the threshold are quarantined or excluded before the model context is built; R4 a model-requested tool call is re-authorised server-side (goal, user authorization, tool permission, allowed arguments) before execution; R5 malicious source content cannot trigger an unauthorised tool call or cross-user disclosure (negative tests); R6 output-side safeguards in answer() retained and tested; no sole dependence on prompt instructions
items.required_tests: held-out injection corpus run in CI; tool-authorization negative tests; cross-user retrieval tests; output-guard tests; per-language injection suite
